h1: The 6 Best Dimmable Smart Plugs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dimmable Smart Plugs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 dimmable smart plugs scored on dimming range, platform support and outdoor use, from Matter models to budget two-packs.
summary: The Leviton Decora Smart Dimmer Plug is the best overall: Wi-Fi without a hub, adjustable fade rate, bulb type settings and Alexa, Google and Siri control. The Tapo P135 kit is the Matter-certified pick with a wireless dimmer button. The Kasa Outdoor Dimmer Plug is the one for patio string lights. Budget buyers should look at the New One and Eva's Light two-packs or the MoesGo.
intro: A smart plug that dims is a different animal from a smart plug that switches. An ordinary plug just cuts power, so it can turn a lamp on and off but will never take it to 30%. A dimmer plug chops the power wave itself, and that is exactly why it only suits lamps designed to be dimmed, not every bulb you own.

That catch explains most of the bad reviews in this category: a flickering, buzzing lamp that is actually a non-dimmable LED. Six dimmable plugs went through the Primea framework here, with the most weight going to dimming control, platform support (Matter, Alexa, Google, Apple) and bulb compatibility, then to extras like outdoor ratings and multipack value.

products.name: Leviton Decora Smart Dimmer Plug D23LP-1RW
products.verdict: A hub-free Wi-Fi dimmer plug with fade control and bulb type settings from an electrical brand.
products.description:
Leviton's second-generation Decora Smart Dimmer Plug runs on Wi-Fi with no hub and works with Alexa, Google and Siri. The standout settings are an adjustable fade rate, which sets how quickly the lamp ramps up or down, and bulb type settings that tune the dimming curve to the lamp. A firmware update adds Matter support.

It beats the Tapo kit because those bulb settings address the flicker problem at the source, while the Tapo's strength is its wireless dimmer button. Compared with the budget two-packs, you pay for a brand known for wall dimmers and better control options.

A clear pick for living room and bedroom lamps. The caveat is that it is a single plug, and Matter is delivered by update rather than out of the box, so check your firmware.
products.idealFor: Anyone dimming living room or bedroom lamps who values fine control.
products.skipIf: You want a two-pack for the lowest total cost.

products.name: Tapo Smart Dimmer Plug Kit P135 KIT
products.verdict: A Matter-certified dimmer plug with two outlets and a wireless dimmer button in the box.
products.description:
The Tapo P135 kit is Matter-certified out of the box, which means it works across Apple Home, Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings. It includes a wireless dimmer button you can stick on a wall or nightstand, so dimming does not depend on a phone. The plug offers two outlets, one left and one right.

It ranks second because the Leviton's bulb settings and fade control give finer tuning, while the Tapo wins on platform breadth and the physical remote. Against the Kasa outdoor plug, it stays indoors only.

Good for apartments mixing Apple and Android phones, where Matter avoids lock-in. Caveat: with two outlets on one plug, you need to confirm that both lamps are dimmable and share the load comfortably.
products.idealFor: Mixed Apple and Android homes wanting Matter and a physical button.
products.skipIf: You need outdoor use or detailed bulb curve settings.

products.name: Kasa Outdoor Smart Dimmer Plug
products.verdict: An IP64 outdoor dimmer plug with long-range Wi-Fi, made for patio string lights.
products.description:
Kasa's outdoor dimmer plug is rated IP64, which covers splashing water from any direction, and uses long-range Wi-Fi to reach a backyard far from the router. It is aimed at dimmable outdoor string lights, with grouping and scheduling, and works with Alexa and Google Assistant.

It ranks third because the other picks are indoor devices with richer platform support, while the Kasa fills a narrow but common need. Unlike the Tapo, it lacks Matter, and unlike the Leviton, it lists no bulb type or fade settings.

Buy it for deck, patio or pergola lights that should dim at dusk and shut off at midnight. Caveat: IP64 is weather resistant, not submersible, so keep the plug off the ground and under an overhang.
products.idealFor: Patio and deck string lights that need dimming outdoors.
products.skipIf: Your lamps are indoors and you want Apple support.

products.name: MoesGo Smart Dimmer Plug
products.verdict: A hub-free 0% to 100% dimmer with random on and off for when you are away.
products.description:
MoesGo offers a 0% to 100% dimming range with no hub, available in a single pack or a two-pack. Two features stand out: a timed dimming schedule that ramps a lamp gradually, and an away mode that randomly switches the light on and off to mimic someone being home. It works with Alexa and Google Assistant.

It ranks fourth because it sits below the Leviton and Tapo on platform breadth, with no Apple or Matter listed. Compared with the two-packs below, the away mode and timed dimming are the real differentiators.

A solid choice for a lamp you want to automate on vacation. Caveat: the full 0% to 100% range can mean flicker at the low end with bulbs that do not dim smoothly, so pair it with dimmable bulbs.
products.idealFor: Travelers wanting lamps to look occupied.
products.skipIf: You rely on Siri or Matter.

products.name: Eva's Light WiFi Smart Dimmable Plug 2 Pack
products.verdict: Two plugs that list LED, CFL and halogen support, with timer and countdown functions.
products.description:
Eva's Light bundles two dimmable plugs with 0% to 100% dimming and a stated compatibility list: dimmable LED, CFL and halogen bulbs. Timer and countdown functions are built in, and voice control works with Alexa and Google Assistant. For a bedroom with two nightstand lamps, a two-pack is the convenient way to set both at once.

It ranks below the MoesGo because it lacks an away mode, but above the New One pack thanks to the explicit bulb list, which tells you what the plug expects at the socket. Against the Leviton you lose bulb type settings and fade control.

A budget option for matching lamp pairs. Caveat: the listing names no hub or Matter support, so check that your voice assistant and router band work before ordering.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms with two lamps that should dim together.
products.skipIf: You want Siri control or a physical dimmer button.

products.name: New One 2 Pack WiFi Smart Dimmer Plugs
products.verdict: A basic two-pack on the Smart Life app and 2.4GHz Wi-Fi with full-range dimming.
products.description:
New One supplies two Wi-Fi dimmer plugs that work through the Smart Life app on 2.4GHz networks, with 0% to 100% dimming and Alexa and Google Assistant voice control. It is the stripped-down option, with the fewest extra features, and its appeal is the price per plug.

It finishes last because the listing offers no bulb-type guidance, no away mode and no Matter or Apple support, and 2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi can be fussy on dual-band routers. Against the Eva's Light pack, the main difference is a less detailed compatibility list.

Choose it for simple lamp pairs where you want the cheapest entry to smart dimming. Caveat: the Smart Life app is a shared white-label platform, so interface polish and firmware support vary.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers adding dimming to two basic lamps.
products.skipIf: You want Siri, Matter or detailed dimming controls.

whatMatters.detail: Dimmer plugs chop the AC waveform to lower brightness, and only dimmable bulbs have the driver circuitry to cope. A non-dimmable LED will flicker, buzz or fail early. Look for a stated list of bulb types, like the LED, CFL and halogen on Eva's Light, and check the bulb's packaging for the word dimmable before plugging it in.

A 0% to 100% range sounds complete, but cheap LEDs often cut out or flicker near the bottom of the slider, so the usable range is narrower than the label. Bulb type settings and fade controls on plugs like the Leviton shape the curve to the lamp. Look for those settings if you plan to run low light levels.

Matter works across Apple, Google, Amazon and SmartThings, so a Matter plug like the Tapo survives a platform switch without re-buying hardware. Others, like the MoesGo and New One, rely on Alexa and Google only. Check the supported assistants and whether Matter is built in or arrives later via an update, as with the Leviton.

Outdoor plugs need an IP rating, because a plain indoor plug on a patio lets moisture reach the relay and dimmer circuit. The Kasa carries IP64, which handles splashes from any direction but not submersion. Look for the IP number on the listing, and mount outdoor plugs off the ground and under cover.

Many cheap plugs only connect to 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, so a router set to 5GHz alone blocks pairing, as with the New One's stated 2.4GHz. Some hub-free models, like the Leviton, work directly with your router. Check the listing for band support and whether a hub is needed, and enable 2.4GHz before setup.

faq.q: Will a dimmer plug work with any lamp?
faq.a: Only with lamps and bulbs designed to dim. The Leviton and Eva's Light list dimmable LED, CFL and halogen support. A non-dimmable LED plugged in will flicker or hum, so check the bulb before buying.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming every LED dims. Even with the best plug, such as the Leviton, a bulb not marked dimmable will misbehave. Match the bulb type setting in the app to the lamp, and test at low brightness.

faq.q: Is the Tapo P135 worth it over the Leviton?
faq.a: If you want Matter and a wireless dimmer button, yes. The Tapo works with Apple, Alexa, Google and SmartThings out of the box, while the Leviton offers finer dimming control and adds Matter by update.

faq.q: How do I set up a hub-free dimmer plug?
faq.a: Plug it in, open the vendor app, connect it to your 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and follow the pairing steps. The Leviton and MoesGo need no hub, while the New One relies on the Smart Life app.

faq.q: Can I use the Kasa Outdoor plug in the rain?
faq.a: It is IP64 rated, which resists splashing from any direction, so rain blowing onto it is fine. Keep it off wet ground and under an overhang where string lights hang, and never submerge it in standing water or snow.

faq.q: Can the plug dim a heater or a fan?
faq.a: No. Dimmer plugs are for lamps and dimmable lighting only, because chopping the power to a motor or heating element damages it and can overheat the plug. None of these listings, including the Tapo and Kasa, supports such loads.

finalTake: The Leviton Decora Smart Dimmer Plug is the best buy for most homes, with fade control and bulb type settings that fix the flicker problem at its source. Choose the Tapo P135 kit if Matter and a physical button matter, and the Kasa for outdoor string lights. Whatever you pick, use a bulb marked dimmable, because the plug cannot fix the wrong bulb.
